Recent work favors improving the objective before aggressively mining the hardest negatives. [Sampled Softmax for Item Recommendation (2024)](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) describes efficient batch-shared negative sampling and shows temperature matters: excessively low temperature lets a few hard negatives dominate gradients. [Scalable Cross-Entropy (RecSys 2024)](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/5392aca9-0bae-4176-9b3a-a8165957ba26) approximates softmax using maximum-inner-product selection of informative catalog items. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) identifies bias from treating the always-present positive like a sampled item; its refined correction handles positive and negative contributions separately. These are transferable objective ideas, not established gains for this BERT4Rec benchmark.

False-negative control argues against unconditional top-score mining. [EMM (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026004090) combines hard and random negatives, refreshes candidates, excludes positive/self IDs, and filters excessively similar candidates. Practical hypothesis for the supplied BERT4Rec: retain masked-target training and appended-mask inference; start with batch-shared uniform sampled softmax, then test a modest mixture of random and semi-hard negatives scored by the same network. Exclude known training positives, padding and mask IDs; deduplicate candidates; warm up before mining and tune temperature conservatively. These safeguards are proposed adaptations, not guarantees that unobserved items are true negatives. Model-dependent hard selection changes the sampling distribution, so uniform-sampling corrections cannot be applied blindly. Keep one jointly trained network per category and select changes solely by macro validation HR@10; the cited evidence does not establish category-specific improvements for Industrial_and_Scientific or Electronics.

---

Recent work supports combining textual content with sequential signals, but does not establish that a lightweight text encoder trained from scratch improves BERT4Rec under this benchmark. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) combines BERT-derived titles, descriptions and reviews with a SASRec-based encoder; its reported Amazon improvements therefore involve a different backbone and unavailable review inputs. [Sequence-level Semantic Representation Fusion (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) argues that simple addition of text and ID embeddings can be ineffective because their representations differ, motivating contextual fusion. These findings support testing learned content integration, without assuming semantic similarity implies purchase compatibility.

For timestamps, [TemProxRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) combines absolute/relative temporal and positional embeddings in self-attention, plus contrastive learning across temporally proximate interactions; it reports gains on its benchmarks. A constraint-compatible experimental hypothesis is one BERT4Rec per category with a small, randomly initialized title/description token encoder, gated content–ID integration, and learned bucketed historical time-gap attention biases, all jointly optimized through masked-item prediction. Preserve reserved-mask inference and final nonpadding readout; exclude target text and unknown target timestamps from inputs. This adaptation is an inference from related work, not a published result for the supplied setting.
